industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the sector rows doing the work: Renewable energy equipment and Test and measurement go to D this week and Electrical equipment, Flow control and Building technology hold D, against Distributors, Diversified groups, Engineered components and Industrial services at C. Danske (26-Nov) has automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries) as data-centre installers peak (Bravida Sell; Kristell, 22-Nov) and Kepler (26-Nov) likes cables (Prysmian) and testing; Goldman's cyclical call names Technology, Retailers and Aerospace and Defence, not capital goods. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Three live holdings (Arteche, IMCD, Sdiptech; 12.93 points). Counter-case for D: the tape and the capital-spending unwind; for B: the automation turn. To D on relative strength F with a hyperscaler guide cut read.

sector.key: O.15. Industrial and chemical distributors and technical trading
sector.why: Neutral, carried. Relative strength B (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior), two readings at B, against no source speaking to distribution. One live holding, IMCD (4.15%, Fitness 89.4, the book's highest); Pool names Beijer Ref (first on the starting score), Azelis, Bunzl, Bossard. Counter-case: two readings at B and the strongest Pool name in the table sitting at Neutral. To B when a source carries a distribution read with relative strength holding B.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the first country-specific evidence since the row was set: Germany's composite PMI is 55.0, a 56-month high (Goldman Economics, 24-Nov; S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov), with automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries; Danske, 26-Nov) and Bunds forecast at 3.1% by end-2027 (Marshall, 22-Nov); the signed Lists statement asks for a country view wherever there is evidence, and this week there is. Eleven Pool stocks are German-listed. Counter-case: one PMI print is one month, the US tariff lands on the EU at 15% inclusive, Stehn's winter energy squeeze applies to the euro area, and the German Pool names (Bayer, Symrise, Evonik, Talanx, Sartorius, Deutsche Borse among them) are global businesses on which a country letter is a blunt instrument. Back to C on a German PMI read under 52 or a second month of euro area services PMIs falling.
